chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazzal, from Hammad ibn Waqid Al-Lahham, who said:

I faced Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) on a road, so I turned my face away from him and passed by. Then I went to him after that and said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! I meet you but I turn my face away, disliking that it would be grievous upon you.' So he said to me, 'May Allah have mercy on you! A man met me yesterday in such and such a place and said, "Upon you be peace, O Abu Abdillah." How good (is your action), but (his pronouncing it in public was) not beautiful.'
ai.seo_question: What is the rationale behind turning away from the Imam in public according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith illustrates the principle of *Taqiyya* (dissimulation) by distinguishing between the validity of a greeting and the wisdom of its public delivery during times of political tension. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates Hammad’s subtle avoidance as a prudent measure to prevent burdening the Imam, while gently correcting the man who greeted him loudly, implying that excessive public display can be less aesthetically pleasing or discreet in context. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing religious observance with situational awareness to protect the community and the Imams from undue attention or harm.
